So when they have started opening and closing daily, wait for them to get to a nice size, the flower should be a bit larger than a travel bottle of alcohol, pick, wash and pat dry. It's best to pick early in the morning when the flower has only semi-opened at peak ripeness.

From there personally, I like to stuff with a four cheese and herb mixture, mainly fresh mozarella, some provolone, a bit of cream cheese and some blue to give of bite.

Chives and parsley are ideal, but other woody herbs like rosemary and thyme play nice as well. Use a kitchen mixer and mix until soft and homogeneous.

Make up a standard tempura batter, or if a light beer batter works well too. Stuff the flowers with the cheese mix, ensuring to remove the stamen as that can cause an allergic reaction to a very small % of people.

Twist off the flower ends lightly, they should be quite soft, be careful not to split the flowers as otherwise your cheese mixture might pop out before the batter has time to solidify in the deep fryer.

Fry at 175 deg C and remove when golden brown. Serve with a simple salad, good olive oil, caremalised balsamic vinegar and flake salt.
